datasource_item.source_question_text:
7. A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0.
B. 𝑣0 cos 𝜃.
C. 𝑣0 sin 𝜃.
D. 0.
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
Q7. A diver launches from the water with speed \(v_0\) at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal. What is the diver’s speed at the maximum height of the trajectory (neglect air resistance)?
A. \(v_0\).
This is incorrect because the vertical component decreases to zero, so the speed generally drops from its initial value.
B. \(v_0 \cos\theta\).
This is correct because at the top the vertical velocity is zero while the horizontal component remains \(v_0 \cos\theta\).
C. \(v_0 \sin\theta\).
This is incorrect because \(v_0 \sin\theta\) is the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at maximum height.
D. 0.
This is incorrect because only the vertical component becomes zero at the top, not the horizontal motion.

B. We can model a delivery truck as a point mass when estimating how far it travels on a highway over tens of kilometers.
This is correct because over long travel distances the truck’s size is negligible compared with the displacement, so a point-mass model captures position change well.

This is incorrect because “neglect air resistance” is effectively the same modeling move as treating the situation like a vacuum for that effect.
D. None of the above is correct.
This is incorrect because option B is a valid approximation for long-range translational motion.
